<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `kernel_config.rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant=enable` (#60710), `_fits_in_memory_budget` treats blocks held by the torch caching allocator as used. Configs that fit fail at load time with `Not enough room in the gpu_memory_utilization budget ...`. This change counts those blocks as free. Port of ROCm/vllm#1411.

## Claims

- Fixes spurious startup failures of the dense prefill cache when the allocator holds cached-free blocks from load-time temporaries.
- Gemma-4-31B AWQ-4bit + MTP-3 on gfx1151: minimum accepted `gpu_memory_utilization` drops from 0.891 to 0.840, and configs in between now start and serve.
- No runtime cost: the check runs only during weight loading and adds no flush or device sync.

## Validation

gfx1151 (Strix Halo, 100 GiB reported), upstream main dc45a5f552 built from source.

Unit tests, `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py -k prefill_dequant`:

- main + new test: `1 failed, 11 passed`
  `FAILED ...::test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant_counts_allocator_cache_as_free - ValueError: Not enough room in the gpu_memory_utilization budget to cache a...`
- this PR: `12 passed`

End to end: `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit`, MTP draft `google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant` (3 tokens), `max_model_len=4096`, `max_num_seqs=1`, `kernel_config={"rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant": "enable"}`; greedy chat prompt "What is the capital of France?".

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.99 | starts | starts |
| 0.87 | `ValueError` at layer check 232/240 | starts, KV 11,035 tokens, "The capital of France is Paris." |
| 0.85 | `ValueError` at layer check 223/240 | starts, KV 8,661 tokens, "The capital of France is Paris." |

Lowest utilization each check accepts (max over the 240 per-layer checks): 0.8912 on main, 0.8402 with this PR. At the peak check, 5.37 GiB of the 81.46 GiB device usage is allocator-cached-free. The 0.85 run, just above the new threshold, still sizes KV and serves, so the relaxed check does not admit configs that cannot fit.

## Details

Blocks the caching allocator keeps after load-time temporaries (checkpoint loading, int4 unpack/dequant scratch) are reused by the next allocation, and KV-cache sizing already excludes them, so the check over-reserved by an amount that depends on allocator state (5.4 GiB here, 15.4 GiB on a build that also loads an int8 lm_head, where the same model failed at 0.99). The check now adds `MemorySnapshot`'s `torch_memory - torch_allocated` to free memory; headroom, min-KV reservation and all-or-nothing behavior are unchanged.

Alternatives considered:
- `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` before or after a failed check: also works, but adds a sync and fresh allocations, and would also run on weight reload and sleep/wake.
- `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`: worse (more cached-free).
- `garbage_collection_threshold`: no effect without a per-process memory fraction, which vLLM does not set.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `_fits_in_memory_budget`. #61193 is a different dense-prefill approach and does not have this check.

AI assistance (Claude) was used. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

nodes.body:
## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
From what I remember, "soft" was removed. Why do we need _fits_in_memory_budget then? If we go oom, I think its fine to fail later on

you're correct that without soft the `_fits_in_memory_budget` doesn't decide anything. It does however print a useful error message and names `rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant` in the message (as opposed to the "KV cache doesn't fit" error). It also fails early and saves time i.e. it fails mid-load instead of after the full load + profile/compile run.

Having said that I am happy to drop this check and rely on the KV cache check. What is your preference?
Does it make sense to add `@pytest.mark.parametrize("min_kv_gib, fits", [(0, True), (8, False)])` tests to guard off CDNA and cuda?

I'm on the fence here as well.  On one hand I think it may be more helpful to users to see that they're not just hitting a kv-cache OOM due to overusage of tokens, and that they're partially caused by the dequant cache.  

My only concern is if we end up raising an error when there might have been space available.  @zohaibm-amd  is that possible?
